title: Engine computer: EMU Black or the EMU PRO already ruled
ask: Should the BP run an ECUMaster EMU Black at about $1,299 with its own MAP sensor and wideband controller (a), or the EMU PRO 8 ruled in D-446 at about $1,849-2,064 (b)?
why:
Camden, 2026-10-17: "now for electrocal do the same the plan must still acount for everything on the base level ... consider lean paths that keep a very clean end finish along with the plan but with the more waves as budget allows"

D-446 chose the EMU PRO when the engine was an LS. Its price, output count, built-in wideband and alternator output were left confirm. The engine is now a 4-cylinder BP, NA now and turbo later.

Read 2026-10-17 at ECUMaster USA's list prices:
- EMU Black $1,299: a built-in 4-bar MAP sensor (to about 43 psi of boost) and a built-in wideband controller for a Bosch LSU 4.2 or 4.9 sensor; drives up to 6 passive or 12 smart coils.
- EMU PRO 8 $2,064 (Katech $1,849): 31 outputs and 24 inputs, two internal LSU 4.9 controllers; a built-in MAP sensor not confirmed.

Both are ECUMaster, so both talk to the PMU-24 over CAN as the plan wants (D-325). The BP needs 4 injector and 2 coil outputs, plus idle, purge, fan, pump, boost and A/C, which the EMU Black covers with room for the turbo.

The answer decides the dash side of the BP leg (K5: ECU pin to cavity) and whether the external MAP-400 (01-engine AI04) and the AEM wideband controller in the Display Unit (electrical WBO) are needed at all.
options:
(a) EMU Black, about $1,299 plus a Bosch LSU 4.9 sensor (about $80-110). Its own MAP sensor and wideband controller mean no external MAP-400 and no separate AEM controller: the Display Unit shows lambda from the ECU on CAN. About $750-1,000 less than (b) all told. Forecloses only an engine needing more outputs than 6 injectors and 6 coils, which no planned stage has.
(b) EMU PRO 8 as D-446 ruled, about $1,849-2,064, with an external MAP sensor if it has none inside. More inputs and outputs than the BP will ever use.
recommend: (a), unless you expect an engine with more than six cylinders one day - then (b)
stops: K5 (the dash side of the BP leg), BP05's ECU pins, and whether parts AI04 and electrical's WBO are bought
